Glossary rules only the compound གསང་སྔགས་ཐེག་པ = 'Mật Chú thừa'. c039 uses 'Mật chú' for bare གསང་སྔགས (pp0123) and for bare སྔགས (p0124 l.1); casing normalised to 'Mật chú' within the chunk. Needs a central ruling, including whether bare སྔགས should differ from གསང་སྔགས.

terms.vi: tương ưng với hàng Thanh văn
terms.note: Viniścayasaṃgrahaṇī quotation, p0124 l.3. ལྡན་པ needs a ruling distinct from the outer དང་ལྡན་པ of the same sentence, which is rendered 'đầy đủ'. 'tương ưng với' chosen so the source's asymmetry against the plain-genitive third item survives; also flagged on the chunk.

p0117, པོ་ཏོ་བའི་དཔེ་ཆོས = 'Thí Dụ Pháp của ngài Potowa'. Rendered literally (དཔེ = thí dụ, ཆོས = pháp). Distinct from the 'tập ngữ lục của ngài Potowa' (c018, c020), which renders a different Tibetan phrase.
p0117. Taken as the Vinayavastu (འདུལ་བ་གཞི); ལུང = āgama, གཞི = vastu. NOT verified — see flags. Occurs 4× in the corpus (p0117, p0165, p0172, p0209), so a ruling is worth making once.
The first member of དལ་འབྱོར alone. Rendered 'sự tự do' to stay inside the fixed phrase 'tám tự do và mười thuận duyên'. Compound དལ་བའི་རྟེན = 'thân y có sự tự do' (རྟེན = thân y, per c005).
p0117, Āryaśūra verse. The negative counterpart མི་དགེ་བཅུ (p0118) = 'mười điều bất thiện'.
p0119 (BCA verse). The source has the metrically shortened བཅོམ་ལྡན, not བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས; same Vietnamese. 'Thế Tôn' is already in use in earlier chunks but has no glossary entry.
p0119, Suhṛllekha — the king Nāgārjuna is addressing. Literally 'lord of men'.
p0118, གཉེན་པོས་མ་བཅོམ་པ = 'chưa bị đối trị phá hủy'.

p0117, Potowa's Dpe chos: རྐྱང་ལ་ཞོན = 'cưỡi lừa hoang'. The Tibetan wild ass (kiang). Translated rather than transcribed; contrast the glossary's གཡག = 'trâu yak', where the simile depended on the animal's name.
p0117, Potowa's Dpe chos. Left in Wylie transcription — the referent could not be established. See flags.

The yoke of the blind-turtle simile, in both the BCA verse (p0119, གཡེངས = 'trôi giạt') and the Suhṛllekha verse (p0119, གནས = 'nằm'). The two verbs are kept distinct in Vietnamese. Note that neither verse says the turtle is blind, so 'rùa mù' is not used.
Recorded only to note that ཕལ་མོ་ཆེ and ཕལ་ཆེར in the same Catuḥśataka verse are both rendered with 'phần đông/phần lớn'; the Tibetan variation is not reproduced.

terms.vi: lấy tinh túy / lòng mong muốn lấy tinh túy
terms.note: Names a section heading (c035 line 21 'Khuyến phát việc lấy tinh túy nơi thân y có tự do'; c039 line 11 'Cách thức lấy tinh túy như thế nào'), so it must be one form. 'tinh túy' is the established form across c035/c038/c039; c037 had drifted to 'tinh yếu' and has been aligned. Recommend status fixed.

SCOPING REQUEST, not a new entry: the existing provisional entry gives only 'hành trạng' with a note that it was made for the biographical sense. At p0119, དེ་ནི་རྣམ་ཐར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ ('chẳng được giải thoát khỏi nó', c037 line 116) is unambiguously the liberation sense — the sentence is about escaping the lower realms. The entry should be scoped to two senses so the sweep does not flag this as drift. Note ཐར་པ alone is already fixed to 'giải thoát'.

Raised by the c037 repair: བདག་གི་སྤྱོད་པ་འདི་འདྲས (p0118) had been rendered 'hạnh nghiệp', importing the fixed ལས = 'nghiệp' into a line with no ལས. Worth a ruling that སྤྱོད་པ never takes 'nghiệp', to keep ལས and སྤྱོད་པ distinguishable. (སྤྱོད་འཇུག as a title is already registered separately.)
Quoted in the closing sentence of the section, p0121. དགེ་བཤེས kept as the title 'Geshe', in transcription like the other Kadam names.
p0120, the setting of Potowa's story.
p0120, the castle in Potowa's story; named twice. Transcribed, not translated (མཁར = fortress/castle). Transcription of ཕྱྭ as 'Cha' is my reconstruction.

Two kinds named at p0120–121: འདོར་བའི་ལེ་ལོ = 'sự biếng nhác buông bỏ', མི་འཇུག་པའི་ལེ་ལོ = 'sự biếng nhác không bắt tay vào'. 'biếng nhác' follows c016 and c031; 'giải đãi' deliberately not used, to keep one form.

terms.vi: sự nhớ nghĩ đến cái chết
terms.note: p0121, where the text defers the topic to a later section; that later section will need the same rendering.
p0121, དལ་འབྱོར་གྱི་ངོ་བོ. Follows c009's use of 'thể tánh'. Kept distinct from རང་བཞིན = tự tánh (fixed).
p0121. Follows the majority precedent (c017, c025, c029, c039). Note c036 renders the same pair 'giai đoạn trước mắt' / 'cứu cánh' — Phase 5 should unify.

terms.vi: hạng khác loại / hạng đồng loại
terms.note: p0121, the two comparison classes in the argument that a happy rebirth is rare.
p0121, སྨོན་ལམ་དྲི་མ་མེད་པས་མཚམས་སྦྱོར་བ — the aspiration prayer that joins cause to result. Rendered flatly; the Tibetan names no object, so none is supplied.

p0120 l.3, qualifying སྙིང་པོ་ལེན་འདོད. Brought into line with the provisional མཚན་ཉིད = "tướng". Flagged per decisions.md: the sense here is "complete in its defining characteristics" (i.e. a fully qualified wish), not "definition", so "định nghĩa" does not apply — but "đầy đủ tướng" is stiff Vietnamese and the compound མཚན་ཉིད་ཚང་བ may deserve its own entry (e.g. "đầy đủ đủ mọi đặc điểm" / "trọn vẹn tướng").

p0120 l.1, spoken by རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་ཆེན་པོ to སྤྱན་སྔ. Obscure colloquialism: བག can point to caution/restraint ("ease off, go a bit gently") or to attentiveness ("put some care into it") — opposite exhortations, and the following clause ("because this leisure and endowment is hard to obtain") reads with either. Left untranslated with both readings flagged inline. Needs a ruling from a reader of Kadampa oral idiom; recurs in the Kadampa anecdote material.

terms.vi: thấy là [hiếm hoi] đến mức cùng tột
terms.note: p0121 l.3, བདེ་འགྲོ་ཙམ་ཡང་སྲིད་མཐར་སྣང་ལ. Elliptical: literally "even a mere happy migration appears at the limit of existence", with no predicate stated. The supplied "hiếm hoi" is now bracketed. A ruling on this idiom would let it be rendered without brackets.

Named here as the antidote to trạo cử. Kept distinct in form from the bare verb སྐྱོ་བ, rendered 'nhàm chán' in the Asaṅga quotation on the same page (and in c033.md), so the shared root stays visible but the technical noun has one fixed form.
p0109, inside the Śrāvakabhūmi quotation: བརྣབ་སེམས་ལ་སོགས་པའི་དྲི་མ་དང་སྙིགས་མ. Kept distinct from འདོད་ཆགས = 'tham' in the next paragraph.
The antidote to trầm một: raising/rousing the mind by seeing qualities. The verb གཟེངས་བསྟོད་པ recurs elsewhere in the book (e.g. བློ་གཟེངས་བསྟོད་ན), so it needs one fixed rendering.
p0110. A monastic teaching/debating college. Rendered plainly; 'pháp hội' was rejected because that is ཆོས་ཚོགས and would lose the scholastic sense on which the argument turns.

p0110, ཆོས་གྲྭའི་བློའི་འཁུལ. NOT a mis-decoding of འཁྲུལ: འཁུལ occurs 6× in the corpus, always in ཡིད་འཁུལ / བློའི་འཁུལ (being convinced, conviction taking hold), against 145 separate occurrences of འཁྲུལ. Recorded so a later chunk does not 'repair' it to 'lầm lẫn'.

p0109, ཚད་ལྡན་དུ་མས་གསུངས་པ. Elsewhere the book uses ཚད་ལྡན adjectivally (ཚད་ལྡན་གྱི་དགོངས་འགྲེལ = authoritative commentaries), so the substantive use here is ambiguous between persons and texts — see flag.
p0110, last sentence. The debate-technical sense (the position stated in order to be examined/refuted) was chosen; see flag for the competing parse.

p0110, ཤིན་ཏུ་ལེགས་ཤིང་མད་པས. Verified against the rendered page at scale 6: the glyph is a plain མ, no ར superscript. The collocation ཤིན་ཏུ་མད་པ occurs 6× in the corpus and ཤིན་ཏུ་རྨད་པ never (རྨད appears 16×, always in རྨད་དུ་བྱུང་བ / རྨད་བྱུང). Read as this edition's spelling of རྨད་པ = marvellous, which fits all six contexts; not normalised in the source.
Already used this way in c006/c007 but with no glossary entry. Kept distinct from རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་ཆེན་པོ = 'bậc Đại Du-già' (a personal name in the glossary).
p0109, hapax in the corpus, inside the Śrāvakabhūmi smith simile. དཔྱད may mean either the craftsman's instruments or his procedure — see flag.

terms.vi: nỗi bất an nơi ý có phiền não
terms.note: p0109, in the Śrāvakabhūmi quotation. Rendered descriptively rather than with 'ưu' so that ཡིད་མི་བདེ་བ stays visibly distinct from སྡུག་བསྔལ = khổ.
Companion to the སྐྱོ་ཤས entry above; the form that appears inside the quoted passage at p0109 (སྐྱོ་བར་བྱས). Registering both is what makes the two-way split in one chunk defensible.

GAP, wording kept per the rule. 3× in c034: ཡོན་ཏན་མཐོང་བའི་བློ, ཉེས་དམིགས་མཐོང་བའི་བློ, ཆོས་གྲྭའི་བློ. Consistent within the chunk, so not drift. Flagging the collision the checker raised: 'trí' overlaps ཤེས་རབ = trí tuệ (provisional) and ཡེ་ཤེས; a neutral 'tâm' or 'ý' may be preferable. This is a high-frequency term and the ruling will require a retro-sweep of whichever chunks used the other form, so decide it early.

UNRULED, not a violation — houseStyle.rules lists only sinh/sanh and phúc/phước. c034 has both spellings. The glossary already licenses 'chánh' inside fixed Sino-Buddhist compounds (Chánh Đẳng Chánh Giác, chánh niệm và tỉnh giác), while 'chân chánh' here is a free adverbial rendering of ཡང་དག་པར. Proposed rule, consistent with the northern register already declared: 'chính' in free/adverbial use (chính yếu, chân chính), 'chánh' retained only inside the fixed compounds already in the glossary. Left untouched in the file pending the ruling.

p0126, Madhyamakahṛdaya verse. Rendered off the precedent in c004, which renders དལ་བ as 'nhàn hạ' (དལ་བའི་རྟེན་བཟང → 'thân người nhàn hạ tốt đẹp'). ཁོམ་པ in the same line = 'sự nhàn hạ'. Deliberately not 'tám nạn', which is a Chinese-derived list-name the Tibetan does not use here.
p0127 and p0128 (×3), of འདུན་པ and of བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས. Rendered descriptively rather than with the compact Sino-Vietnamese 'bất tạo tác'.
p0129, paired with ཕྱིན་དྲུག = sáu ba-la-mật.
p0129. Built on the glossary's ལྟུང་བ = đọa tội.
p0129, listed after རྩ་ལྟུང and ཟག་པ་ཆུང་འབྲིང. Established Sino-Vietnamese 惡作.
p0129, དེའི་བསླབ་བྱ་རྣམས (the precepts of the aspiration vow). Kept distinct from བསླབ་པའི་གཞི = học xứ, which is already in the glossary.
p0129. c007 already used 'nghi quỹ phục hồi' for the related idea; this is the bare compound.
p0128, བསག་སྦྱང་གི་སྒོ་དུ་མ. The Tibetan names no objects (merit / obscurations), so none were supplied.
p0129. Built from the glossary's འཇུག་པའི་སེམས = tâm nhập and སྡོམ་པ = luật nghi.
p0129. ཆོ་ག = nghi quỹ, following c007; སྨོན་པ = tâm nguyện, following the glossary's སྨོན་པའི་སེམས.

p0129, སྐྱོང་རེས་ཀྱིས་དེ་དག་དྲན་པར་བྱས་ནས. Rendered provisionally as 'trong từng phiên hành trì'. See flag — the compound occurs only twice in the whole corpus (p0129 and p0940) and I could not verify the sense.

p0129, ཟག་པ་ཆུང་འབྲིང་དང་ཉེས་བྱས་རྣམས. Rendered 'những sai phạm bậc nhỏ, bậc trung'. Deliberately NOT 'lậu' (āsrava), which is ཟག་པ's usual sense but does not fit a list of vow infractions between རྩ་ལྟུང and ཉེས་བྱས. See flag.

terms.vi: có thể được vận dụng tùy ý
terms.note: p0129, of the mind on a virtuous object. Kept distinct from ལས་སུ་རུང་བ = kham nhậm, already in the glossary.

terms.vi: sự tự do / (cảnh) không tự do
terms.note: No standalone entry exists, though decisions.md §4 (དལ་འབྱོར) settles the register and c035.md already renders མི་ཁོམ་བརྒྱད = "tám cảnh không tự do", ཁོམ་པ = "sự tự do" (source/clean/lamrim.txt 1001-1005). c040 line 15 has now been aligned to that. Needs a ruling so the "nhàn hạ / nhàn mãn" register cannot resurface.

Glossary registers only the contracted རྒྱལ་སྲས → "Phật tử" (provisional), while རྒྱལ་བ is status fixed → "Đấng Chiến Thắng". The uncontracted form at p0126 (རྒྱལ་བའི་སྲས་སམ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ) has no ruling; rendering it "Phật tử" substitutes Buddha for Victor where the source spells the epithet out. Wording KEPT pending a central ruling on whether the long form follows རྒྱལ་སྲས or the fixed རྒྱལ་བ (e.g. "con của Đấng Chiến Thắng").

terms.vi: tăng thượng sinh / quyết định thắng
terms.note: Line 64 (p0127). Matches c036 and c039. No entry for either.

Lines 104-105 (p0129). Glossary has the separate lemma སྨོན་པའི་སེམས = tâm nguyện, but bare སྨོན་པ standing for the aspiration vow has no ruling. Currently rendered with the supplied noun bracketed. A ruling should say whether bare སྨོན་པ in vow contexts may take "tâm nguyện" unbracketed.

terms.vi: sai phạm bậc nhỏ, bậc trung
terms.note: Line 110 (p0129). First occurrence. Note the readability collision: "bậc" is reserved by decisions.md §3 for the three capacities (bậc hạ/trung/thượng), which occur throughout this same chunk. A ruling should either license "bậc" here or pick an alternative (e.g. "sai phạm nhỏ và vừa").

Line 94 (p0129). Obscure form, first occurrence, currently rendered as "in each session of maintaining/practice" (སྐྱོང = sustain a practice, རེས = turn/alternation). Rendering kept but it is NOT certain; needs a ruling and, if the reading is wrong, a correction.

p0167 l.2, cited as the source for where animals dwell. Rendered with the established Sino-Vietnamese name of the Maulī Bhūmi section of the Yogācārabhūmi (本地分), consistent with the glossary's ཉན་ས = Thanh Văn Địa and བྱང་ས = Bồ-tát Địa. The term's first occurrence in the book is p0160 (chunk c050), so the two must be reconciled.
p0166 l.6-7, in the Suhṛllekha verse སྲེད་ཟད་པ, rendered 'sự dứt sạch ái'. Kept as bare 'ái' rather than 'tham ái' so that འདོད་ཆགས / ཆགས་པ stay separable.
p0166 l.11-12, རང་གི་སྒོ་གསུམ་གྱི་ཉེས་སྤྱོད = 'ác hạnh nơi ba cửa của chính mình'. Left literal, not expanded to 'thân khẩu ý', because the verse two lines later spells out ལུས་ངག་ཡིད separately.
p0167 l.12, paired with མི = 'loài người'.

terms.vi: điều thiện đưa đến tịch tĩnh
terms.note: p0167 l.7 (verse form ཞི་འགྱུར་དགེ་བ) and l.14-15 (commentary form), where the text itself glosses it as མྱང་འདས་འཐོབ་པའི་དགེ་བ = 'điều thiện đạt được niết-bàn'. One Vietnamese phrase for both forms so the gloss visibly attaches to the verse. ཞི་བ = 'tịch tĩnh', kept clear of the ཞི་གནས = tịnh chỉ set.
p0167 l.12, one of the items the word སོགས in 'བརྡེག་སོགས' is said to include.
p0167 verse, ལྕག་དང་ལྕགས་ཀྱུ. Whip/lash. No ruling; part of the unruled animal-goad instrument list. Kept.
p0167 verse, ལྕག་དང་ལྕགས་ཀྱུ. Iron hook / elephant goad. No ruling; rendered literally rather than as 'câu móc'. Kept.

p0167, fifth item in ལྕག་དང་ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་གདབ་པས་བཏབ་སྟེ་བཀོལ and in རྡོག་པས་བཏབ་སྟེ་བཀོལ་བ་ནས་གདབ་པས་བཏབ་སྟེ་བཀོལ་བ་ལྔ. NOT an implement: a verbal noun of འདེབས་པ, the same root as the following བཏབ, so the Tibetan is literally 'driven by having struck with a striking'. The commentary counts five and assigns the fifth to གླང (ox), but never names a tool. Rendered non-committally and flagged; a ruling is needed on whether to keep a verbal-noun rendering or adopt a bracketed supplement.

p0145-p0147, five occurrences (འཆི་བདག་དྲུང་དུ་སྐྱེལ / འཆི་བདག་གིས་བཅོམ་ནས / འཆི་བདག་དྲུང་དུ་འགྲོ / ལམ་རྣམས་ཐམས་ཅད་འཆི་བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་བཀག / འཆི་བདག་བརྩེ་བ་མེད་པ་ཅན). No glossary entry existed. Rendered 'Tử thần' (personified, capitalised) so it stays distinct from the ordinary noun འཆི་བ = 'cái chết', which occurs beside it in the same sentences. It also occurs in c045 (p0142, the sub-topic heading འཆི་བདག་ངེས་པར་འོང་...), which is not yet translated — the two must agree.

p0145. Rendered from the Tibetan components (རྒྱ་ཆེར = đại/quảng, རོལ་པ = du hý), following the project practice for titles with no verified Vietnamese form (cf. དགྲ་ནག, ཐོས་པའི་ཚོམས). Note that the Chinese-derived Vietnamese tradition knows this sūtra as *Kinh Phổ Diệu* / *Kinh Phương Quảng Đại Trang Nghiêm*; neither was adopted because the source names the Tibetan title. Flagged.

terms.vi: Thuyết Ngăn Dứt Bốn Điên Đảo
terms.note: p0146 and p0147, cited twice. Rendered literally from the Tibetan on the pattern already fixed for མི་ཁོམ་པ་བརྒྱད་ཀྱི་གཏམ → 'Thuyết về Tám Cảnh Không Tự Do' (གཏམ = thuyết). ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག = điên đảo, འགོག་པ = ngăn dứt. Sanskrit title not verified.

p0147. Mātṛceṭa's letter. The source writes ཀཱ་ནི་ཀ (not ཀ་ནི་ཥྐ); the Sanskrit name is restored as Kaniṣka in the Vietnamese. Rendered 'Thư Gửi X' rather than on the བཤེས་སྤྲིངས → 'Thân Hữu Thư' pattern, because a personal name does not read as a Sino-Vietnamese compound; if the project prefers uniformity the alternative is 'Kaniṣka Thư'.

p0146. Built from the fixed བཞི་བརྒྱ་པ → 'Tứ Bách Luận' plus the pattern of བཤེས་སྤྲིངས་འགྲེལ་པ → 'Chú Giải Thân Hữu Thư'. The text cites a verse *quoted inside* the commentary (དྲངས་པ་ལས), not the commentary's own words; rendered 'trong [đoạn] được trích dẫn nơi...' to preserve that.

p0147, inside the Jātakamālā verse (ཀུ་མུ་ཏ་ཡི་དཔལ). Sanskrit plant name left in Latin transcription, following the project practice for Sanskrit proper names; 'hoa' supplied so the Vietnamese parses. No gloss ('sen đêm', 'súng trắng') added inside the quotation.

terms.kind: doctrinal term - unregistered, collides with ཁམས་གསུམ
terms.note: c046 L24 (p0145 l1, Lalitavistara verse). No entry; glossary.json has སྲིད་པ -> hữu (provisional). "Ba cõi" is already carrying ཁམས་གསུམ (c044 L54, source p0139), so two distinct Tibetan terms converge on one Vietnamese phrase - the same pattern decisions.md §5 records for the reverence family and the same collision already flagged for འགྲོ་བ/སེམས་ཅན. Wording kept pending a central split (e.g. ཁམས་གསུམ -> ba cõi, སྲིད་གསུམ -> ba hữu / tam hữu).

terms.kind: doctrinal term - governing term of the section, unregistered
terms.note: c046 L19, L24, L32 (p0145 l1). Standard and consistent throughout the chunk and the section headword ངེས་པར་འཆི་བ་བསམ་པ depends on it; simply not recorded in glossary.json.

Raised by this repair. ཁྱེད is the honorific second person; c046 L35 (p0145 l1, Kamapa to a disciple) had "ngươi", now "ông". But c049 L53 renders ཁྱེད་རྣམས (p0152, the voice in the Reviving Hell) as "Các ngươi", and "ngươi" appears for second-person address in c014/c017/c020/c022/c048/c052/c056/c057/c060/c064 whose Tibetan I have not checked. A ruling is needed on how ཁྱེད (honorific) and ཁྱོད (plain) are kept apart in Vietnamese, otherwise the distinction is decided ad hoc per chunk.
p0139, cited as མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ཆེན་པོ་ལས (no མདོ in the Tibetan), so rendered as a bare title *Đại Bát Niết Bàn*. Distinct from the glossary's མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ = niết-bàn (the state).

p0139, cited bare as ཚོམས་ལས་ཀྱང (the abbreviation of ཆེད་དུ་བརྗོད་པའི་ཚོམས). glossary.json already carries two of its chapters as ཐོས་པའི་ཚོམས = *Phẩm Văn* and མཛའ་བཤེས་ཀྱི་ཚོམས = *Phẩm Thân Hữu*; the whole-work title had no entry. Chosen after the Chinese canonical 法集要頌經. Owner should confirm this harmonises with the 'Phẩm X' chapter titles.

terms.vi: mục đích của bậc trượng phu
terms.note: p0139, སྐྱེས་བུའི་དོན་བསྒྲུབ་པའི་དུས. Uses the སྐྱེས་བུ = 'bậc' register already fixed for the three capacities.
p0139, in the Udānavarga verse ཆོས་རྣམས་སྨིག་རྒྱུ་འདྲར་ཤེས་ནས. Plain-Vietnamese 'quáng nắng' chosen over Sino-Vietnamese 'dương diệm' because it stands inside a verse simile.
p0141, sa-bcad heading opening the fourfold structure of the death meditation (རྩ་བ་གསུམ / རྒྱུ་མཚན་དགུ / ཐག་བཅད་པ་རྣམ་པ་གསུམ). Fixed here because it heads the next several chunks.
p0141, in the same fourfold structure as རྩ་བ་གསུམ.
p0141, in the same fourfold structure as རྩ་བ་གསུམ.

terms.vi: bậc trượng phu (in 'mục đích của bậc trượng phu')
terms.note: p0139 l.3, སྐྱེས་བུའི་དོན་བསྒྲུབ་པའི་དུས. No ruling for bare སྐྱེས་བུ; glossary.json rules only compounds (སྐྱེས་བུ་ཆུང་ངུ/འབྲིང/ཆེན་པོ -> bậc hạ/trung/thượng, fixed; སྐྱེས་བུ་དམ་པ, སྐྱེས་བུ་ཐ་མ, སྐྱེས་བུ་མཆོག). KEPT per the repair rule, but flagged as genuinely contestable: decisions.md §3 deliberately strips 'sĩ' from the three-capacity names to keep them plain, and 'trượng phu' re-imports a heroic/masculine gloss that སྐྱེས་བུ alone does not carry. Plainer candidates: 'mục đích của con người' / 'mục đích của kẻ trượng phu' / 'nhân sinh mục đích'. This is the only occurrence of 'trượng phu' in translation/, and སྐྱེས་བུའི་དོན recurs at p0213, p0259, p0441, p0524 — one ruling here settles four later chunks.

p0139 l.1, བདུད་ཀྱི་མེ་ཏོག་མཚོན -> 'binh khí hoa của ma'. No standalone entry; glossary.json carries only compounds built on the same word (བདུད་ཚར་བཅད་པའི་སྔགས -> 'chú tiêu diệt ma', བདུད་ཀྱི་རིས་ཀྱི་ལྷ -> 'chư thiên thuộc dòng ma'). KEPT — consistent with those, simply unrecorded.

Occurs 5× in this chunk, incl. two sa-bcad headings. glossary.json fixes bare འཇིག་རྟེན = 'thế gian', but this compound names the next life, and 'thế gian đời sau' would be unreadable in the headings. Paired in the text with འཇིག་རྟེན་འདིར = 'nơi thế gian này' and ཚེ་འདི = 'đời này', where I kept 'thế gian' for the standalone use. Needs a ruling that the compound is exempt from the fixed entry.

Heading s056 (p0136). Built on the glossary's བཀའ་དྲིན་རྗེས་སུ་དྲན་པ = 'tùy niệm ân đức', so རྗེས་སུ་དྲན་པ = tùy niệm. Deliberately kept distinct from the bare འཆི་བ་དྲན་པ = 'sự nhớ nghĩ đến cái chết' already in glossary.json — see flag; the two Tibetan forms are almost certainly free variants for one practice.

p0136, འགྲོ་བ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་བདེ་སྡུག = 'khổ vui của hai thú' — the two destinies བདེ་འགྲོ / ངན་འགྲོ, which glossary.json already renders thiện thú / ác thú. Kept apart from the glossary's འགྲོ་བ = chúng sinh, which is a different sense of the same word.
p0136, ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་བཞི = 'bốn điên đảo'. No glossary entry; glossary has only ལོག་རྟོག = tà chấp, a different word.
p0137, རྙེད་པ་དང་བཀུར་སྟི་ལ་སོགས་པ་ལ་ཆགས་པ་དྲག་པོ. Follows c028/c036, which already use 'tham đắm'. Kept distinct from the glossary's འདོད་ཆགས = tham ái.
p0137, སྡང་བ་དྲག་པོ. Follows c026/c033. No glossary entry for སྡང་བ or ཞེ་སྡང.
p0137, ཉེས་དམིགས་ལ་རྨོངས་པའི་གཏི་མུག = 'si mê, [tức] sự mê muội đối với lỗi hại'. Follows c012/c016.
p0137. Follows c016 (p0055, ×2), which is the only prior occurrence in the translated corpus. Sino-Vietnamese 'tật đố' was the alternative but c016 has already set 'ganh tị'.
p0137. A third kind of ལེ་ལོ beside the two already recorded (འདོར་བའི་ལེ་ལོ, མི་འཇུག་པའི་ལེ་ལོ); keeps 'biếng nhác' per that entry.
p0137. Occurs exactly once in the whole 978-page corpus. བྲེ་མོ = idle/frivolous; rendered non-technically.
p0137, བཟའ་བཏུང་ལ་སོགས་པའི་རྣམ་གཡེང. No glossary entry.

p0137, in the list of unwholesome karmas, with དེ་དང་ཉེ་བ = 'những [tội] gần với vô gián' (the near-ānantarya). glossary.json has མཚམས་མེད = 'Vô Gián' but only as a hell-name (p0081); this is the karma, so 'tội' is supplied in brackets.
p0136, ×2 — the structural term of this section (the conceit of permanence is the first 'door of harm').
p0137, ལུས་སྲོག་ཡུན་རིང་དུ་གནས་སུ་རེ་བ.
p0137, ཉེས་སྤྱོད་སྡིག་ལྟུང. Contraction of སྡིག་པ + ལྟུང་བ; expanded to two nouns, using the glossary's ལྟུང་བ = đọa tội.

p0137 l.1, བརྩོན་པ་ཆེན་པོས་ཚུལ་བཞིན་དུ་བསྒྲུབ་པ. Bare ཚུལ་བཞིན has no entry; the only ruling is the compound ཚུལ་བཞིན་ཡིད་ལ་བྱེད་པ = 'như lý tác ý' (provisional), which entails ཚུལ་བཞིན = 'như lý'. The chunk's earlier 'đúng như pháp' was corrected to 'như lý' on that basis, but a ruling on the bare adverbial ཚུལ་བཞིན་དུ is still needed so later chunks do not re-decide it.

p0136 l.7, three sa-bcad items: ...འཆི་བ་རྗེས་སུ་དྲན་པ་བསམ་པ་དང༌ / ...བདེ་སྡུག་བསམ་པའོ. The existing བསམ་པ = 'ý lạc' (provisional) is scoped to bare བསམ་པ as the partner of སྦྱོར་བ (āśaya), and the chunk correctly keeps 'ý lạc' for the nominal use in the top heading ཆུང་ངུའི་བསམ་པ་སྦྱང་བ་དངོས. No ruling covers the verbal 'to contemplate' use; 'nghĩ đến' kept. A ruling would stop a mechanical Phase 5 sweep reading the split as drift.

p0136 l.3 and l.5, འཇིག་རྟེན་ཕྱི་མ་དོན་གཉེར་གྱི་བློ. The existing དོན་གཉེར་བ = 'tha thiết cầu tìm' (provisional) is scoped to the third of the three qualities of a listener. c039 renders this sense 'mong cầu' too, so the usage is consistent against an unruled context; kept.
p0136 l.11, l.15. Bare འཆི་བ has no entry; the compound འཆི་བ་དྲན་པ = 'sự nhớ nghĩ đến cái chết' (provisional) IS fixed and the chunk follows it exactly, so 'cái chết' is the consistent bare form.

p0137 l.1, གཉིད་རྨུགས་དང་བྲེ་མོའི་གཏམ. No entry of its own; it appears only inside the note on སྒྲིབ་པ = 'triền cái' (p0085 five-hindrances list), which does not rule on the Vietnamese for the compound itself.

The head term of this whole section (~30× in c055 alone) and of c056–c058. No glossary entry exists; 'quy y' is already in live use in c028/c040. Related forms as rendered here: སྐྱབས = 'chỗ quy y' (the object), སྐྱབས་འགྲོ་སྦྱང་བ = 'tu tập quy y' (སྦྱང་བ = tu tập, following the glossary's བློ་སྦྱང་བ = tu tâm), སྐྱབས་སུ་འོས་པ = 'xứng đáng làm chỗ quy y', སྐྱབས་སུ་མཆི (verse) = 'con xin quy y'.
p0176. Follows c005's *Bát Thập Tán* for བསྟོད་པ་བརྒྱད་ཅུ་པ — same Sino-Vietnamese numeral + Tán pattern. The author is not named in the source, so none is supplied.

p0177. Rendered literally rather than with a Sino-Vietnamese coinage (Quy Y Thất Thập), following the precedent recorded for སྨོན་ལམ་བདུན་ཅུ་པ = 'Bảy Mươi Lời Nguyện'. 'Kệ' supplies a word the Tibetan བདུན་ཅུ་པ does not have, exactly as 'Lời' does in that precedent; if the precedent is revisited both should move together. The author (Candrakīrti) is not named in the source and is not supplied.

p0176, introduced as བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱི་གླང་པོས. Occurs nowhere else in the translated corpus. 'Trần-na' (陳那) is the established Vietnamese form; this departs from c005's practice of romanised Sanskrit for Indian masters (Rāhulagupta, Śīlarakṣita) on the same grounds that Maitreya is 'Di-lặc' there — a ruling is needed on where the line falls.

p0175, the second of the two sub-topics of section 6.2.3.1.1.2 (its own section is c059+, so this is only the announcing outline). Built on the glossary's དད་པ = 'lòng tin'. The bare verb ཡིད་ཆེས་པ at p0176 is rendered 'tin chắc'. See flag: 'xác tín' sits uncomfortably close to 'xác quyết', which the corpus uses for ངེས་པ.

terms.vi: Tu tập quy y, cửa ngõ chân chính để thể nhập giáo pháp
terms.note: Outline s070, path 6.2.3.1.1.2.1, level 2 → '##'. དམ་པ = 'chân chính' per the glossary's བཤེས་གཉེན་དམ་པ entry; སྒོ = 'cửa ngõ' per c040; བསྟན་པ = 'giáo pháp' per glossary; འཇུག་པ = 'thể nhập' per c040.

terms.vi: Nương tựa vào phương tiện đạt an lạc nơi thế gian đời sau
terms.note: Outline s069, path 6.2.3.1.1.2, level 1 → '#'. འཇིག་རྟེན་ཕྱི་མ = 'thế gian đời sau', following c039 line 33 (འཇིག་རྟེན་ཕྱི་མའི་མཐོ་རིས → 'các cõi cao của thế gian đời sau'); བསྟེན་པ = 'nương tựa' per the glossary's འདུ་ཤེས་དྲུག་བསྟེན་པ.

terms.vi: Nhân do nương vào đó mà quy y / Đối tượng quy y do nương vào [nhân] ấy
terms.note: Outline s071 and s072, path 6.2.3.1.1.2.1.1–.2, level 3 → '###'. The paired གང་ལ / དེ་ལ is kept visible; 'nhân' is bracketed in the second because the Tibetan དེ refers back to the cause named in the first.

p0176. 'nghiệp đen' already occurs in c033 line 82, so this follows the corpus rather than coining 'hắc nghiệp'. Note the tension with the glossary's དཀར་པོའི་ཆོས = 'bạch pháp' — a ruling should decide whether the ལས pair follows the ཆོས entry into Sino-Vietnamese or the ཆོས entry follows these into plain Vietnamese.

terms.vi: cúng dường bằng tài vật / cúng dường bằng tu hành
terms.note: p0177, the fourth reason. The contrast is the point of the sentence, so both halves are rendered by the same frame. Distinct from the glossary's བླ་ན་ཡོད་པའི་མཆོད་པ / བླ་ན་མེད་པའི་མཆོད་པ = 'cúng dường hữu thượng / vô thượng' (p0087), which is a different opposition; the two pairs should not be collapsed.

p0177, དབང་ཕྱུག་སོགས་ལ་མེད་པས — the non-Buddhist god offered as a counter-example to the Buddha. Must NOT take the glossary's རྣལ་འབྱོར་དབང་ཕྱུག = 'Du-già Tự Tại' or འཇིག་རྟེན་དབང་ཕྱུག = 'Thế Tự Tại'; this is a third, separate use of the bare word.

terms.vi: chỗ quy y không hư dối
terms.note: p0176–p0177. བསླུ་བ་མེད་པ = non-deceptive; 'không hư dối' rather than 'không lừa dối' to keep the register of an epithet of the Buddha.

p0176, inside the Dignāga verse (འདོད་ཆགས་ལ་སོགས་མི་བཟད་པའི་ཆུ་སྲིན). Rendered generically rather than with the Sanskrit 'ma-kiệt-ngư', since the verse uses it as an image of a devouring sea-creature, not as a named species.
p0177, of the Buddha's ཐུགས་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ. Literally 'without near-and-far'; the Sino-Vietnamese 'thân sơ' carries exactly that.

NOT a new gap but a defect in the existing glossary: two conflicting provisional entries already exist - ཡིད་འཁུལ = 'thấm vào tâm' (note explicitly covers p0176 སྐྱབས་འགྲོ་ཡང་ཡིད་འཁུལ་བ་ཞིག་འོང) and ཡིད་འཁུལ་བ / བློའི་འཁུལ = 'sự tin nhận (của tâm trí)'. c055 now uses 'thấm vào tâm', the form whose note names this site. The two entries need merging into one ruling before p0185 (the third occurrence of the same clause).

p0177 l.7 and l.11. No entry. glossary.json fixes སྙིང་རྗེ = 'bi' and registers སྙིང་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ = 'đại bi' (provisional), so the current rendering collapses the honorific ཐུགས་རྗེ family into the སྙིང་རྗེ family. Kept as rendered (no ruling), but decisions.md §5 set the precedent of splitting near-synonyms to keep them separable; a ruling is needed on whether ཐུགས་རྗེ་ཆེན་པོ takes its own form (e.g. 'lòng đại bi' vs 'đại bi') or is deliberately merged.

No entry anywhere in glossary.json, despite being the headword of section 6.2.3.1.1.2.1 and governing c055-c059. Rendering is uncontroversial and kept: verbal/abstract སྐྱབས་འགྲོ = 'quy y', nominal སྐྱབས (the object) = 'chỗ quy y'. The ruling should fix that two-way split explicitly so later chunks do not coin 'nơi nương tựa' or 'quy mạng'.

No entry. c055 has it twice with two forms: ཡིད་ཆེས་ཀྱི་དད་པ (p0175 l.5) -> 'lòng tin xác tín', and ཡིད་ཆེས་པ (p0176 l.1) -> 'tin chắc rằng'. Both kept, since no ruling exists and the second is a finite verb where the first is a nominal modifier. But ཡིད་ཆེས་ཀྱི་དད་པ names sibling section 6.2.3.1.1.2.2 (c065), so one fixed stem is needed before that chunk. དད་པ = 'lòng tin' (provisional) is followed correctly here.

p0177 l.9, opposed to ཟང་ཟིང་གི་མཆོད་པ = 'cúng dường bằng tài vật' (ཟང་ཟིང = 'tài vật' follows its entry correctly). No entry. Kept, but glossary.json renders སྒྲུབ་པ as 'tu tập' inside སྒྲུབ་པའི་ཆོས = 'pháp thuộc phần tu tập', so 'tu hành' is an unregistered second form of the same element; the ruling should pick one.
p0156, first of the four divisions of hell. Built on the existing glossary entry སེམས་ཅན་དམྱལ་བ = 'địa ngục hữu tình' plus ཆེན་པོ.
p0156, second of the four divisions. 近邊地獄, the established Sino-Vietnamese name; ཉེ་འཁོར = surrounding/adjacent.
p0156, third of the four divisions. Kept as the plain adjective (གྲང་བ = lạnh) rather than the Sino-Vietnamese 'hàn băng', which adds 'băng' (ice) that the Tibetan does not have.

p0156, fourth of the four divisions. ཉི་ཚེ་བ = partial/particular/limited; p0165 defines these as 'established by the individual karma of one, two, or many', which supports the 'particular' reading. The conventional Vietnamese name is 'địa ngục cô độc' (孤獨地獄, solitary), which translates a different word. See flag - needs a central ruling before p0165 is translated.
p0157, first of the eight great hells. Established Sino-Vietnamese 等活, matching the Tibetan sense 'revive again' (the sky-voice ཡང་སོས་པར་གྱུར་ཅིག puns on the name).
p0157, second great hell. 黑繩 = 'black cord', exactly ཐིག་ནག.
p0157, third great hell. 眾合.
p0158, fourth great hell. 號叫.
p0158, fifth great hell. 大號叫.
p0158, sixth great hell. 炎熱. Only as the hell-name; the ordinary adjective ཚ་བ stays 'nóng'.
p0158, seventh great hell. 極炎熱.
p0157-p0158, the hell-guardians. Recurs throughout this section.
p0156. No glossary entry existed; 'quy y' already used five times in the translated corpus.

p0156, twice: once in prose beside ང་རྒྱལ (ngã mạn) and once in the Bodhicaryāvatāra verse. Given its own word so it stays separable from ང་རྒྱལ / ཁེངས་པ, both of which the glossary already assigns to 'ngã mạn'.
p0156, twice. Kept distinct from སྐྱོ་བ = 'nhàm chán' (glossary) and སྐྱོ་ཤས = 'lòng yểm ly', which both appear on the same page inside the quoted verse.

p0156 and again at p0444 (ལམ་གྱི་གནད་མཐའ་དག་བསྡུས་པའི་སྡོམ་ཆེན་པོ). Read as སྡོམ 'summation, epitome' rather than སྡོམ་པ 'vow', on the strength of the parallel with བསྡུས་པ / འདུས་པ in both occurrences. See flag.
p0158, in ལྕགས་ཀྱི་གསལ་ཤིང and ལྕགས་ཀྱི་གསལ་ཤིང་རྩེ་གསུམ་པ (three-pointed).
p0158, ལྕགས་ཟངས་ཆེན་པོ་འགྱུར་བྱེད་བསྐོལ་བས་གང. Taken as a caustic/corrosive liquid ('that which transforms'). See flag - not securely identified.
p0159, in ཁ་དང་ལོག་མ་དང་རྒྱུ་མ (mouth, gullet, intestines) burnt by molten copper.
p0157, the simile བུར་ཤིང་འཚིར་བ་བཞིན་དུ = 'as sugarcane is pressed'.

Bare སྡིག་པ has no entry (only སྡིག་གྲོགས / སྡིག་པའི་གྲོགས་པོ = bạn ác is registered). Within c049 it splits two ways in ~20 lines: prose L12 renders སྡིག་ལྟུང as 'tội lỗi và đọa tội', while the Bodhicaryāvatāra verse L29 renders སྡིག་ལ་འཛེམ as 'Kiêng dè điều tội'. ལྟུང་བ = đọa tội is registered and correctly used in both places, so the split is only on the སྡིག་པ member. Kept as written pending a ruling; a ruling should close whether the verse register may use 'điều tội' or must match the prose.

p0142. Follows the glossary's existing X-ཀྱི་ཚོམས pattern (ཐོས་པའི་ཚོམས = Phẩm Văn, མཛའ་བཤེས་ཀྱི་ཚོམས = Phẩm Thân Hữu). It is the impermanence chapter of the same collection that bare ཚོམས names; see the flag on that pairing.
p0142, first occurrence in the corpus (only page where it appears). The Tibetan writes no མདོ; 'Kinh' supplied for the Vietnamese to read as a title, on the precedent of the མངལ་དུ་འཇུག་པ entry.

Fourth of the འཇིགས་པ་ཆེན་པོ་བཞི in the Rājāvavādaka quote (p0143): རྒ་བ / ན་བ / འཆི་བ / རྒུད་པ = già / bệnh / chết / suy vong. Glossed in the sūtra itself as what destroys ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པ, i.e. decline of fortune, not physical decay.
p0142, in the stock triad སེམས་ཅན / སྲོག་ཆགས / འབྱུང་པོ. Kept distinct from chúng sinh (སེམས་ཅན, fixed).
p0142, third member of the same triad. Rendered generically; see flag — bhūta can also mean elemental spirits, and the Tibetan here does not disambiguate.
p0144. The prose spells it ཕྱུགས་རྗིས and the verse four lines later ཕྱུགས་རྫི; both translated the same way (see flag).

terms.vi: Phẩm Vô Thường (line 18) vs. Pháp Tập Yếu Tụng (line 99)
terms.kind: cited title - conflict needing a central ruling
terms.note: p0142 l.5 མི་རྟག་པའི་ཚོམས་ལས rendered "Phẩm Vô Thường", following the pattern already fixed for ཐོས་པའི་ཚོམས = Phẩm Văn and བཤེས་ཀྱི་ཚོམས = Phẩm Thân Hữu (name only the chapter, because only the chapter is named in the Tibetan). p0144 l.3 bare ཚོམས་ལས rendered "Pháp Tập Yếu Tụng", the corpus precedent (7 prior uses in c044/c047/c064/c065/c079). Both halves follow existing precedent, so no entry was departed from - but the same collection is named two ways within three pages, and the back-references at lines 27 and 37 ("cũng trong bộ ấy", for དེ་ཉིད་ལས) point at the Phẩm form. Needs one ruling reconciling the chapter-name pattern with the bare-ཚོམས title (e.g. chapter-qualified = Phẩm X, bare ཚོམས = Pháp Tập Yếu Tụng, stated explicitly), plus an entry for མི་རྟག་པའི་ཚོམས itself. Text left as is pending that ruling.

p0142 l.7 སྔགས་ལ་སོགས་པས་བཟློག་ཏུ་མེད་པ (line 46) and three times inside the Rājāvavādaka quotation (རྫས་དང་སྔགས་དང་སྨན་, p0142 l.7 and p0143 l.1; lines 54, 58, 63). The glossary rules only གསང་སྔགས་ཐེག་པ, རིག་སྔགས = minh chú and སྔགས་པ. The རིག་སྔགས note records "chú thuật" for bare སྔགས in the Bodhicaryāvatāra verse at p0115; the གསང་སྔགས entry records c039 using "Mật chú" for bare སྔགས at p0124 l.1 and explicitly asks for a ruling. c045 follows the "chú thuật" precedent, which also suits this context (mundane spells listed beside རྫས goods and སྨན medicine, as means of warding off death). The split remains unsettled and needs the ruling the གསང་སྔགས entry already requested. Text kept.

The existing entry glosses བསམ་པ as "ý lạc" (āśaya, provisional, paired with སྦྱོར་བ). Every occurrence in c045 is the verbal-noun sense: p0142 l.1 ...མི་ཕན་པ་བསམ་པའོ (line 11), the section heading ངེས་པར་འཆི་བ་བསམ་པ (line 14, p0142 l.3), p0142 l.5 ...བཟློག་ཏུ་མེད་པ་བསམ་པ་ནི (line 16), p0143 l.3 ...ཡོད་པ་བསམ་པ་ནི (line 71), plus p0144 l.3 དཔེ་དུ་མའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསམ (line 93) - all rendered "quán xét". That is the correct reading, but the entry is unscoped, so a naive sweep reads it as a violation. Needs the two senses split the way མཁས་པ (nominal vs. adjectival) already was: āśaya-sense = ý lạc, verbal-noun sense = quán xét. Text kept.

terms.vi: Cách thức quy y bằng bao nhiêu điều
terms.note: sa-bcad heading s073, path 6.2.3.1.1.2.1.3, at p0178 last line. ཇི་ཙམ་གྱིས = 'by how much / by what means'; the section then enumerates four things by which one counts as having gone for refuge. Rendered to keep the enumerative sense; see flags.
Not yet in glossary.json despite governing this whole division. Verbal forms rendered 'quy y'; སྐྱབས་སུ་འོས་པ = 'xứng đáng làm nơi quy y'; སྐྱབས་སུ་འཛིན་པ = 'nhận làm nơi quy y'.
p0178, སྐྱབས་གནས་བཟང་པོ = 'đấng quy y tốt lành'. Personal here (the Buddha), so 'đấng' rather than 'nơi'; bare སྐྱབས as an object is rendered 'nơi quy y'.

p0178, p0179 (བསྡུ་བ་ནས་གསུངས་པ, ×2). The source writes only the bare abbreviation བསྡུ་བ. Aligned to the existing glossary entry གཏན་ལ་དབབ་པ་བསྡུ་བ = Nhiếp Quyết Trạch. This is an expansion of an abbreviation, not something the Tibetan spells out — see flags.

terms.vi: Tán Thán Đấng Đáng Tán Thán
terms.note: p0178 and p0181. Rendered from the Tibetan components (བསྔགས་འོས = đấng đáng tán thán, བསྔགས་བསྟོད = tán thán). Not verified against an existing Vietnamese edition.
p0179, source of the long body-marks praise. Rendered literally (དཔེ = thí dụ, per the glossary's དཔེ་ཆོས = Thí Dụ Pháp; བསྟོད་པ = tán). Sanskrit original not identified — see flags.
p0180. Numeral title, rendered on the pattern of the glossary's བླ་མ་ལྔ་བཅུ་པ = Ngũ Thập Tụng về Thượng Sư.

The three honorific doors, here as the section labels སྐུའི་ཡོན་ཏན / གསུང་གི་ཡོན་ཏན / ཐུགས་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན = 'công đức của thân / của ngữ / của ý' (p0179–p0181). No glossary entry exists for any of the three.

p0181, མཁྱེན་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན and ཐུབ་པའི་མཁྱེན་པ. Deliberately NOT 'trí tuệ' (= ཤེས་རབ, which occurs in this same chunk at p0180) and not bare 'trí' (= ཡེ་ཤེས, which occurs in the Varṇārhavarṇa verse on p0181). Needs a ruling; see flags.

terms.vi: các tướng hảo và tùy hình hảo
terms.note: p0179. Standard Sino-Vietnamese pair. Note the collision risk with the glossary's provisional མཚན་ཉིད = tướng and མཚན་མ = tướng.
p0181, twice (ལག་མཐིལ་དུ་སྐྱུ་རུ་ར་བཞག་པ, and inside the Varṇārhavarṇa verse). Standard Sino-Vietnamese transcription 庵摩勒.
p0180, Satyakaparivarta verse. Kept distinct from the glossary's སྟོན་པ = đấng Đạo Sư, which also occurs in this chunk (p0178, and སྟོན་པ in the Varṇārhavarṇa verse).
p0180, Satyakaparivarta verse.
p0180. Rendered transparently so ཆོས = Pháp stays visible per the fixed-set entry, rather than the compact Sino-Vietnamese 'pháp luân'.
p0180, Śatapañcāśatka verse, as the destroyer of the snake of ཞེ་སྡང.
p0180. No glossary entry; paired in the same verse with འདོད་ཆགས = tham ái (provisional) and གཏི་མུག = si mê at p0181.
p0180 and p0181, twice, both in the Śatapañcāśatka. The eye-disease image; rendered concretely rather than as abstract 'vô minh'.

terms.vi: ban cho sự an ủi / an ủi
terms.note: p0179 (ཕྱག་གིས་དབུགས་འབྱིན་མཛད་པ) and p0181 (ཕོངས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་དབུགས་འབྱིན). Same verb, rendered with 'an ủi' in both.

p0179, the third of the four ways one counts as having gone for refuge, paired with གཞན་དུ་མི་སྨྲ་བ = 'không tuyên xưng nơi nào khác'. 'thừa nhận' chosen over 'phát nguyện', which would add a vow the Tibetan does not write.
p0178, Varṇārhavarṇa verse, སྤྱི་ཡི་རྩ་ལག་བཟང་པོ = 'bậc thân thuộc tốt lành chung cho tất cả'.

No entry for the compound; text kept ("các thế giới", p0180 l.3). Needed because འཇིག་རྟེན is fixed = "thế gian" and bare འཇིག་རྟེན་ན fourteen lines later is correctly "thế gian" - only an explicit compound entry licenses the head-term appearing two ways on one page. Recommend registering འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས = "thế giới" so the Phase 5 consistency sweep does not flag it.

terms.skt: lakṣaṇa (the major marks of a buddha)
terms.note: No entry; text kept. Two rulings needed. (a) p0179 l.7 མཚན་དང་དཔེ་བྱད་བཟང་པོ is "tướng hảo và tùy hình hảo" in prose but plain "các tướng" / "tướng bánh xe" in the verses - the 好 in "tướng hảo" answers to བཟང་པོ, which stands over དཔེ་བྱད only, so the established Sino-Vietnamese pair "tướng" + "tùy hình hảo" (or "tướng hảo" + "tùy hình hảo" as a fixed doublet) should be chosen once. (b) "tướng" is already the provisional Vietnamese for both མཚན་ཉིད (lakṣaṇa) and མཚན་མ (nimitta); with this term, three distinct Tibetan words collapse onto one Vietnamese word. The མཚན་མ entry already proposes a split - this term should be decided together with it.
No entry; text kept (p0179 l.7). Registered alongside མཚན above, since the pair is what the ruling has to cover.

Glossary has ལེགས་གསུངས (with final sa) = "lời khéo giảng", provisional, keyed to a p0051 verse. Here the source spells ལེགས་གསུང and the frame is ལྡན: ཁྱོད་ཀྱི་གསུང་ནི་ལེགས་གསུང་ལྡན། Applying the registered head noun literally yields "Lời của ngài đầy đủ lời khéo giảng", which repeats "lời" for གསུང and ལེགས་གསུང in one clause. Text kept as "đầy đủ sự khéo giảng" and referred for a ruling that covers the ལྡན construction - e.g. one entry ལེགས་གསུང(ས) = "lời khéo giảng", with "sự khéo giảng" licensed where the sentence's subject is already གསུང.
p0172 (the syllable ཚ is on p0171, དམྱལ on p0172). Paired with གྲང་དམྱལ. Rendered descriptively rather than 'nhiệt địa ngục' so the pair reads plainly; combines with the glossary's དམྱལ་བ = địa ngục.
p0172, paired with ཚ་དམྱལ.

p0172–p0173, the central figure of the Vinayavastu story. Tibetan is patronymic ('son of Maudgalya'); rendered with the established Sino-Vietnamese transcription 目犍連, as A-nan is for ཀུན་དགའ་བོ (already in glossary).
p0173. Rendered from the Tibetan components (གཞལ་མེད = vô lượng, ཁང = cung/điện) rather than the flatter 'thiên cung', which would import 'thiên' the Tibetan does not write here.
p0173, contrasted in the same sentence (a vimāna with no ལྷའི་བུ, full of ལྷའི་བུ་མོ), so the pair must stay visibly matched.
p0173, the sound of the emanated devas.

p0173. NOT verified — see flags. Rendered from components (ཡང་དག་པར་ལྡན་པ = samyukta = tương ưng; ལུང = āgama = A-hàm), consistent with the glossary reading ལུང = āgama in ལུང་གཞི = Luật Sự. Occurs only here in the whole corpus, so one ruling settles it.

p0173, vocative address by Maudgalyāyana to the two novices. Confirmed as an address, not a name, by the two other corpus occurrences (p0475, p0478), where it opens direct speech to a stranger. Rendered from the components (བཞིན = diện, བཟང = hiền). See flags.

p0173, the simile for saṃsāra (ཟོ་ཆུན་བརྒྱུད་མོའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་འཁོར་བར་བྱ་དགོས). Rendered literally (ཟོ་ཆུན = gàu múc nước, བརྒྱུད་མོ = chuỗi nối nhau) rather than as 'bánh xe nước', so the image of buckets going down and up stays. Sole occurrence in the corpus.

p0173, འགྲོ་བ་ལྔའི་འཁོར་བ. Uses 趣 = thú to match the glossary's བདེ་འགྲོ = thiện thú / ངན་འགྲོ = ác thú, rather than the glossary's provisional འགྲོ་བ = chúng sinh, which does not fit a count of destinies.

p0174, the Kadam master quoted at length. Left in Tibetan transcription like the other Kadam names (Dromtönpa, Potowa, Geshe Dolpa). Occurs 6× more in the corpus (p0205, p0345, p0350, p0509, p0976), so worth fixing once.
p0172–p0173, Maudgalyāyana's address དགེ་ཚུལ་གཉིས. Not registered; 'sa-di' follows c002 line 16.
p0172–p0173, four occurrences. Not registered.
p0172, ལྕགས་ཟངས་ཆེན་པོ་གཉིས་ཁོལ་བ.
p0172–p0173, twice (ཉིན་མོ་སྤྱོད་དུ་འགྲོ་བའི་ས / ཉིན་མོ་སྤྱོད་པའི་གནས་གཞན). Rendered literally and identically both times; see flags — the technical sense of the Vinaya term is not established here.
p0173, བློ་ཚོད་ཀྱང... — the measure by which one judges whether the meditation has taken. Rendered descriptively; interacts with the glossary's unsettled བློ entry.
p0174, Bodhicaryāvatāra verse (ཀུན་ཏུ་ཡི་མུག་འགྱུར). Kept apart from སྐྱོ་བ = nhàm chán, a different word already registered.
p0174, Bodhicaryāvatāra verse. Literally 'the flesh of panic emerging'; rendered as the panic showing in the staring eyes.
p0174, of redirecting previously accumulated virtue by means of aspiration prayers (སྨོན་ལམ་གྱིས་ཁ་བསྒྱུར་བ). Not 'hồi hướng', which would import བསྔོ་བ.

terms.vi: đầu não nóng ran / bật dậy giật thót
terms.note: p0174, two colloquial reduplicated expressions in Neusurpa's spoken advice. Rendered for effect; see flags — neither is attested elsewhere in the corpus.

p0173, l.46. KEPT — no ruling. Two open questions for the entry: (a) བཟང = good/excellent, not 'hiền' (gentle/kind), so 'diện hảo' / 'thiện diện' may be closer; (b) unclear whether this is a descriptive vocative to the two novices or a proper epithet/name.
p0172 (ཡིད་འབྱུང་བར་གྱིས་ཤིག) and p0173 (ཡིད་བྱུང་ནས), l.19-20 and l.48. Both spellings appear in the source and were rendered alike; the entry should cover both.

p0174, l.65/69/74. The glossary fixes the NOUN བསམ་པ → 'ý lạc'. The finite verb needs its own ruling so it is not pulled toward 'quán tưởng' (visualisation) or toward the noun; 'tu tập' stays reserved for བསྒོམ.

p0172, l.17. Sister of a male ego, no relative age marked. Vietnamese forces a choice between 'chị' and 'em'; the neutral compound avoids asserting either. Worth a standing ruling since kinship terms recur in the Vinaya narratives.

p0131, Candrakīrti; the swan-king verse (MAv VI, closing verse of the chapter). Established Sino-Vietnamese title (入中論) used, following the precedent set for Bảo Tánh Luận and Trung Quán Tâm Luận. The literal Tibetan would be 'Nhập Trung Quán'.

p0130. Atiśa's own commentary on the Bodhipathapradīpa. Built on the glossary's ལམ་སྒྲོན = *Đạo Đăng*; འགྲེལ་པ rendered 'chú giải' rather than the corpus's 'luận giải mật ý' (which translates དགོངས་འགྲེལ, a different thing).

terms.vi: Lược Tập Pháp Tu Đạo Đại Thừa
terms.note: p0132, Atiśa. Rendered from the Tibetan components (ཐེག་ཆེན = Đại thừa, ལམ = đạo, སྒྲུབ་ཐབས = pháp tu, བསྡུས་པ = lược tập). No established Vietnamese title found.
p0132, Atiśa. Built from ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན = định (glossary), ཚོགས = tư lương (glossary), ལེའུ = phẩm — the pattern of the glossary's བདེན་པ་པོའི་ལེའུ = 'phẩm Đế Giả'.
p0130, twice. ཀུན་རྫོབ = thế tục per the glossary's ཀུན་རྫོབ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་སེམས་བསྒོམ་པ note; བདེན་པ = đế. Bare ཀུན་རྫོབ in the MAv verse rendered 'thế tục' without 'đế', since the verse omits བདེན་པ.
p0130, twice. Follows the glossary's དོན་དམ་པ = thắng nghĩa (provisional). Deliberately not 'chân đế', so the pair with thế tục đế stays morphologically parallel.
p0130. No bare entry in glossary.json (only སྒྲུབ་ཐབས compounds). Used in ཐབས་ཀྱི་ཆ = 'phần phương tiện' and ཐབས་ཤེས་ཡ་བྲལ = 'phương tiện và trí tuệ tách rời nhau'.

p0130, paired with བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས = 'tư lương phúc đức' (c024). 'trí' not 'trí tuệ', per the glossary's ཡེ་ཤེས = trí, because ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཆ = 'phần trí tuệ' occurs in the same sentence. See flag — the usual Vietnamese is 'tư lương trí tuệ'.

terms.vi: du-già hữu tướng / du-già vô tướng
terms.note: p0131, the two yogas of the lower tantra classes. མཚན་མ = tướng per the glossary's provisional entry; རྣལ་འབྱོར = du-già.

terms.vi: du-già của sinh khởi thứ đệ / du-già của viên mãn thứ đệ
terms.note: p0131. 'sinh khởi thứ đệ' / 'viên mãn thứ đệ' already used in c006 and c009 ('hai thứ đệ'); kept rather than c007's 'giai đoạn sinh khởi' / 'giai đoạn viên mãn'. The corpus carries both forms — needs one ruling.
p0131, contrasted with རྩ་བའི་ལྟུང་བ / རྩ་ལྟུང = 'đọa tội căn bản' (glossary). Built from ལྟུང་བ = đọa tội and ཡན་ལག = chi.

terms.vi: bộ mật tục có nguồn gốc đáng tin cậy
terms.note: p0131. རྒྱུད་སྡེ = bộ mật tục (glossary); ཁུངས་མ rendered with the same phrase c005's section heading uses for ཆོས་ཁུངས་བཙུན་པ ('giáo pháp có nguồn gốc đáng tin cậy').
p0132, in the Atiśa verse. ལྷག་པ = tăng thượng per the glossary's ལྷག་པའི་བསམ་པ = 'tăng thượng ý lạc'; ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས = giới (fixed).
p0131. Follows the glossary's ཐུན་མོང་བ = 'cộng thông' (of paths and vows).
p0130 prose and the p0131 MAv verse. The bodhisattva as swan-king flying on the two wings of the two truths.

p0132, ལམ་རིམ་གྱིས་ཀྱང་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་འཁྲིད་པའོ. Rendered with the same two words the fixed title བྱང་ཆུབ་ལམ་རིམ་ཆེན་མོ = 'Bồ-đề Đạo Thứ Đệ Quảng Luận' uses. See flag — which lam rim is meant is not stated.

l.24 ཀུན་རྫོབ་བདེན་པ → "thế tục đế", l.25 and l.31 དོན་དམ་པའི་བདེན་པ → "thắng nghĩa đế" (p0130 l.3). Components ཀུན་རྫོབ = thế tục and དོན་དམ་པ = thắng nghĩa are licensed; བདེན་པ itself has no entry at all — the glossary's own བདེན་པ་མཐོང་བ note already asks for one. Rendering is conventional and stable within the chunk; registration owed.

l.62, p0132 l.3 ལམ་རིམ་གྱིས་ཀྱང་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་འཁྲིད་པའོ, italicised as a title. glossary.json registers only བྱང་ཆུབ་ལམ་རིམ་ཆེན་མོ; the only supporting note is under རིམ་པ་གཉིས ("ལམ་རིམ = Đạo Thứ Đệ in the book title"). Two questions in one entry: (a) is bare ལམ་རིམ here a specific work (Atiśa's/Gampopa's lineage lamrim texts, alongside ལམ་སྒྲོན in the same sentence) or a generic reference to the lamrim genre; (b) if generic, it must lose the italics. Text kept pending the ruling. Interacts with the existing རིམ་པ gap (thứ đệ vs trình tự).

terms.vi: sinh khởi thứ đệ / viên mãn thứ đệ
terms.note: l.58 (p0131 l.3) and l.60 (p0132 l.1). glossary.json has a རིམ་པ་གཉིས note referring to "generation and completion stages" but no entry for either stage by name. House style "sinh" is respected. Registration owed; interacts with the རིམ་པ = thứ đệ / trình tự gap.

l.19-20, p0130 l.3 ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ནམ་སེམས་ཀྱི་བསླབ་པ — the text offers it as an alternative name for the fixed ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་གྱི་བསླབ་པ = "định học", so both must appear and stay distinct. No entry for the སེམས་ form; registration owed.

l.108, p0132 l.3 ཡོངས་སུ་འཛིན་ལས་རྒྱབ་ཀྱིས་ཕྱོགས. No entry. Rendered component-faithfully (ཡོངས་སུ = trọn vẹn, འཛིན = nắm giữ); the Sino-Vietnamese "nhiếp thọ" is the conventional alternative and the ruling should pick one, since འཛིན alone is elsewhere the ego-grasping verb (cf. བདག་གཉིས་སུ་འཛིན་པ, l.14).

terms.vi: cõi trời Tứ Đại Thiên Vương
terms.note: p0160. The source writes རིགས་བཞི at first mention and རིས་བཞི at second within the same sentence; both rendered identically. See flag.
p0161. Formed on the pattern of the glossary's བསྐལ་ཆེན = đại kiếp.
p0161, p0163. The established Sino-Vietnamese 近邊地獄.

p0163, mentioned once and never described. Rendered literally (ཉི་ཚེ་བ = partial, particular) rather than with the conventional 孤獨地獄 / 'địa ngục cô độc', which asserts solitariness the Tibetan does not say. See flag.
p0161, first of the four neighbouring hells.
p0161; glossed by the text itself as ཕྱི་སའི་འདམ་རོ་ལྟར་མནམ་པ = 'vũng bùn phân bốc mùi hôi thối như xác chết'.

terms.vi: dòng sông Không Lội Qua Được
terms.note: p0161, p0162. Rendered literally from the Tibetan (རབ = ford, མེད = without) rather than with the Sanskrit name, since the Tibetan itself is a translated name. See flag.

terms.vi: khu rừng có lá là gươm

terms.note: p0162, ལྕགས་ཀྱི་ཤིང་ཤལ་མ་ལིའི་ཚལ = 'rừng cây śālmalī bằng sắt'. Kept as the Sanskrit loanword, as the Tibetan does; no settled Vietnamese tree-name found.
p0161, the creatures in the corpse-swamp; the text marks it as a name (ཞེས་བྱ་བ).

p0163. The eight cold-hell names are rendered literally throughout, because the passage's entire content is an etymological gloss of each name (blisters, bursting, colour, number of splits); a transliterated Sanskrit or Sino-Vietnamese name would sever the link the text is making. See flag.
p0163. The text says this and the next two are named from the manner of uttering sounds.
p0163. The interjection is kept in transcription rather than translated ('than ôi'), since the text says the name comes from the sound uttered.
p0163. Same reasoning as the previous entry.
p0160, Thân Hữu Thư verse: བྱེ་བ་ཕྲག་བརྒྱར = 'trăm câu-chi'. Transliteration chosen over 'ức', whose value is unstable in Vietnamese usage.
Recurs throughout p0160-p0163.
p0163, Bổn Sinh verse. Rendered literally; the verse does not say what is denied, so no object was supplied.

terms.bo: ཡང་སོས / ཐིག་ནག / ཚ་བ / རབ་ཏུ་ཚ་བ / ཉེ་འཁོར་བ / ཉི་ཚེ་བ
terms.skt: Saṃjīva / Kālasūtra / Tapana / Pratāpana / utsada / pradeśika
terms.vi: Đẳng Hoạt / Hắc Thằng / Viêm Nhiệt / Cực Viêm Nhiệt / địa ngục cận biên / địa ngục cá biệt
terms.note: Hot-hell and hell-class names, p0160–p0163. Internally consistent and in agreement with c049/c051; only མནར་མེད → A-tỳ is currently registered. Registration gap, not drift — kept as-is.

terms.bo: ཆུ་བུར་ཅན / ཆུ་བུར་རྡོལ་བ / སོ་ཐམ་ཐམ་པ / ཀྱི་ཧུད་ཟེར་བ / ཨ་ཆུ་ཟེར་བ / ཨུཏྤལ་ལྟར་གས་པ / པདྨ་ལྟར་གས་པ / པདྨ་ལྟར་གས་པ་ཆེན་པོ
terms.skt: Arbuda / Nirarbuda / Aṭaṭa / Hahava / Huhuva / Utpala / Padma / Mahāpadma
terms.vi: Bọng Nước / Bọng Nước Vỡ / Răng Đánh Lập Cập / Kêu "kyi hud" / Kêu "a chu" / Nứt Như Hoa Ưu-bát-la / Nứt Như Hoa Sen / Nứt Như Hoa Sen Lớn
terms.note: The eight cold hells, p0163 l3. Descriptive Vietnamese names throughout, with the two onomatopoeic ones left in transliterated Tibetan inside quotation marks. Consistent with c049/c051; unregistered. Kept as-is pending a single ruling for the whole set.

Three different strategies for Sanskrit plant and flower names inside one chunk: roman Sanskrit (p0162 l1, l3), Sino-Vietnamese transliteration (p0163 l3), and translation (p0163 l3). Each is defensible on its own — 'Hoa Sen' is fully naturalised in Vietnamese, 'Ưu-bát-la' is the established Buddhist transliteration, śālmalī has neither — but the corpus needs a stated policy so Phase 5 does not read the mixture as drift. Nothing changed.

p0162 l3, twice (ལག་ན་དབྱུག་པ་དང་མཆིལ་པ་དང་རྒྱ་བཟུང་བ; མཆིལ་པའམ་རྒྱས་ཕྱིར་ཕྱུང་ནས). UNCERTAIN, and this uncertainty was never flagged. The ordinary sense of མཆིལ་པ is 'spittle'; the implement reading rests only on the context (paired with དབྱུག་པ 'staff' and རྒྱ 'net', and used ཕྱིར་ཕྱུང 'to pull them out'), which supports a hook or a snare but does not decide between them — the parallel Yogācārabhūmi passages list ཞགས་པ 'noose/snare' in this slot. Kept 'móc câu' rather than swapping to an equally unevidenced 'dây thòng lọng', since no glossary ruling exists and swapping would just move the guess. Needs a ruling plus an 'unsure' flag on the chunk.

c050 spells the numeral 'ngàn' throughout ('một ngàn, hai ngàn, ... ba vạn hai ngàn do-tuần'); c049 spells the same numeral 'nghìn' for the same kind of measurement. houseStyle.register is northern but its rules list only sinh/sanh and phúc/phước, so there is no ruling. Corpus counts: ngàn 16 (c050, c053, c062, c072, c077, c079) vs nghìn 2 (c049 only) — c050 follows the majority and c049 is the outlier, so nothing changed here. A houseStyle rule is needed so the Phase 5 sweep can settle it; strictly, northern register favours 'nghìn', which would make c050 and five other chunks the ones to sweep.

Nāgārjuna, cited twice (p0150, p0151). No glossary entry. Rendered from the Tibetan components (རིན་ཆེན་ཕྲེང་བ = precious garland → 寶鬘 Bảo Man) plus 'Luận', following the pattern already used for བཞི་བརྒྱ་པ → Tứ Bách Luận. The Chinese-canon title 寶行王正論 (Bảo Hành Vương Chính Luận) was deliberately NOT used, because it renders a different title from the one the Tibetan writes. Needs owner confirmation.

p0149, cited as bare ཚོམས་ལས, i.e. the whole collection, not a chapter. The glossary so far has only chapter names (ཐོས་པའི་ཚོམས = Phẩm Văn, མཛའ་བཤེས་ཀྱི་ཚོམས = Phẩm Thân Hữu), where ཚོམས = phẩm. Here the established Sino-Vietnamese title of the work (法集要頌經) is used instead, on the precedent of མཛོད = Câu-xá. NOT 'Kinh Pháp Cú', which is a different text.
p0150. c026 rendered the plain མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ as *Niết-bàn*; here the Tibetan writes ཆེན, so 'Đại' is added rather than dropped. Registered so the two forms stay distinguishable.
p0150-p0151 (སྙིགས་མ་ལྔ་ཤིན་ཏུ་བདོ་བའི་དུས). Standard Sino-Vietnamese 五濁. བདོ་བ rendered 'tăng thịnh'.

p0150, opening the Đại Niết-bàn quotation. Built on the glossary's འདུ་ཤེས = tưởng, on the same descriptive pattern as སྣང་བའི་འདུ་ཤེས = 'tưởng về ánh sáng'. Kept distinct from the glossary's འཆི་བ་དྲན་པ = 'sự nhớ nghĩ đến cái chết'.
p0150 (གནོད་པ་དེ་དག་ནི་རང་དང་ལྷན་སྐྱེས་སུ་ཡོད་པས). Established Sino-Vietnamese 俱生.
p0151, listed among the life-extending practices weakened in the degenerate age.

p0148, six occurrences, contrasted with འཇིག་རྟེན་འདི = 'thế gian này'. Follows the nearest precedent, c039 line 33 (འཇིག་རྟེན་ཕྱི་མའི་མཐོ་རིས → 'các cõi cao của thế gian đời sau'), and keeps the fixed འཇིག་རྟེན = thế gian visible rather than collapsing the compound to the bare 'đời sau' that appears in c010/c021/c024/c026/c029/c035/c036/c038. The corpus is split on this; a ruling would need a sweep.

p0150 དེ་ལྲ་ཡང་འདས་ཆེན་ལས། No entry. Distinct short name from མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ behind c026's 'Niết-bàn' (p0082), so the corpus now carries two unregistered Vietnamese titles for nirvāṇa-sūtra citations. Text left unchanged. Ruling needed before p0232, where འདས་ཆེན recurs; it should decide both names together.

p0150–p0151 སྥིགས་མ་ལྔ་ཤིན་ཏུ་བདོ་བའི་དུས། First occurrence anywhere in translation/. No entry. Text left unchanged ('ngũ trược' is the established Sino-Vietnamese). Note the glossary already has སྥིགས་མ alone = 'cặn bả/cấu' senses at p0107–p0109, so the compound needs its own line rather than being read off that.

c047 uses 'Quán chiếu rằng…' in all four headings (ནམ་འཆི་ངེས་མེད་བསམ་པ and its three subdivisions). Its direct sibling འཆི་བ་ངེས་པར་འཆི་བ་བསམ་པ is 'Quán xét' in c045, 'Tư duy' in a c046 sub-heading, 'Quán xét' again in c048. glossary.json rules on བསམ་པ only as the noun āśaya = 'ý lạc' paired with སྦྱོར་བ, which does not govern this use. Text left unchanged. One ruling then a c045–c048 sweep.

p0168, the cause of preta rebirth (སེར་སྣ་ཤས་ཆེར་བསྟེན་པ་རྣམས). No glossary entry. Sino-Vietnamese 慳吝 chosen over 'xan tham' (which imports ཆགས་པ, not in the Tibetan) and over the colloquial 'keo kiệt/bỏn sẻn'. Will recur in the dāna sections, so it needs pinning centrally.

p0168 and p0171, the recurring rubric that closes each realm's description (ཚེའི་ཚད་ནི།). Sino-Vietnamese 壽量: ཚེ = thọ, ཚད = lượng. Structural — it will appear once per realm through the whole ངན་འགྲོ section.

terms.vi: sự che chướng bên ngoài / bên trong / nơi chính [đồ ăn thức uống]
terms.note: p0168-p0169, the threefold division of pretas. IMPORTANT: glossary.json already fixes སྒྲིབ་པ = 'triền cái' (nīvaraṇa, the five hindrances). That sense is impossible here — this སྒྲིབ་པ is a physical obstruction to obtaining or swallowing food, so it is rendered 'sự che chướng'. The glossary entry needs a scope note, or this becomes a false consistency hit in Phase 5. Also: in the third member the Tibetan writes only ཟས་སྐོམ་ལ་སྒྲིབ་པ (no qualifier); 'chính' is supplied to keep it distinguishable from the first two. See flag.
p0169, in the Câu-xá Thích quotation: ཡི་དྭགས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་ནི་གཤིན་རྗེ. Rendered with the established Sino-Vietnamese title rather than transliterated.
p0169, the reference point for the depth of the preta realm. Established Sino-Vietnamese 王舍城.

p0170, Candragomin's Letter to a Disciple, cited at length. Formed on the precedent of བཤེས་སྤྲིངས = Thân Hữu Thư (親友書); 弟子書. NOTE the tension: glossary has སློབ་མ = 'người học trò' (provisional), deliberately kept off 'đệ tử'. That ruling is about the common noun; this is a fixed text title. If the project wants strict alignment the title would have to be 'Thư Gửi Người Học Trò', which no Vietnamese source uses. See flag.
p0168, a named class of preta (ཞེས་བྱ་བ marks it as a name). Rendered literally; kept in quotation marks in the body so it reads as a designation.

p0169, the second named class of preta, glossed by the text itself as བཤང་གཅི་ཟ་ཞིང་འཐུང་བ (eating and drinking excrement and urine). ལན་ལིན rendered by the text's own gloss rather than guessed at etymologically.
p0168 (prose, the inner-obstruction pretas) and p0169 (Suhṛllekha verse, མགྲིན་པ་ནས་ལྦ་བ་བྱུང་བ). The verse fixes the location as the throat, so 'bướu cổ' rather than a generic 'bướu'.
p0169, ཏ་ལ་ཡ་ཐོག་བསྐམས་པ་ལྟ་བུ. Transliterated as is conventional in Vietnamese Buddhist texts; ཡ་ཐོག read as the upper part/crown.
p0170, Śiṣyalekha verse. Standard Sino-Vietnamese transliteration 栴檀.
p0170, Śiṡyalekha verse: ཙནྡན་ལོན་པ་སྔོ་འཁྲུངས་མ་ལ་ཡར་སོང་ན. Identified as the sandalwood mountain on the evidence of ཙནྡན in the same line. 'núi' is supplied, since the Tibetan writes only the name.
p0171, closing paragraph (མེ་མ་མུར་དུ་ལག་པ་བཅུག་ནས). Distinguished from མདག་མ, also 'than hồng' in this chunk (p0170); if the two need to stay separable, one of them must change.
p0171, Śiṣyalekha verse: ཚ་བས་ཉེན་ལ་བུ་ཡུག་ཀྱང་ནི་ཚར་འགྱུར.
p0170, མྱ་ངམ་ཉིད་དུ་འགྱུར. The corpus elsewhere has མྱ་ངམ་ཐང and མྱ་ངམ་གྱི་ཕྱོགས, so the word will recur.

p0171 line 1, Śiṣyalekha: `ཚྭ་ཚྭ་རྡོ་རྗེའི་ཕ་བོང་རྣམས་འཕྲོ`. Syntactically an item in the list of things flying from the cloud (iron-arrow rain, smoke, embers, vajra boulders, lightning-garlands), so a falling substance — hail / sleet / gravel are all plausible, none decisive. Left untranslated in brackets rather than guessed. Needs a ruling.

No entry. p0169, Suhrllekha: `དམངས་རིགས་འགས་ནི`. NOTE THE COLLISION: glossary.json already has `སྨེ་ཤ་ཅན` (caṇḍāla) = 'kẻ hạ tiện'. Two distinct low-caste words are converging on the same Vietnamese and should be split by a ruling before Phase 5's consistency sweep.

p0152, with the epithet རྣལ་འབྱོར་གྱི་དབང་ཕྱུག = 'bậc Du-già Tự Tại' (following c005). Transcribed exactly as the Tibetan letters give it (ཨཱ་ནན་ཏ = Ānanta), not silently corrected to the attested Sanskrit form. Shortened to ཤྲི་ཛ་ག་ཏ་མི་ཏྲ = 'Śrī Jagatamitra' at p0153.
p0152 verse, vocative addressing a king. Rendered literally (ས = đất, བདག = chúa tể) rather than flattened to 'đức vua'.
p0153 verse, vocative to a king ('sole deity'). Coined; no established Vietnamese form. See flag.
p0155, Nāgārjuna verse. Same Vietnamese as the glossary's དུད་འགྲོ = 'bàng sinh' (which also occurs in this chunk at p0154); the two Tibetan words are synonyms and are deliberately collapsed.
p0154, Potowa's ངེད་ཀྱི་སྣང་སེལ. Kadam idiom for what clears away this life's appearances. Rendered descriptively; no compact Sino-Vietnamese form chosen.
p0153–p0154, འཇིག་རྟེན་ཕྱི་མ་ཕན་ཆད་ཀྱི་གཏན་བདེ. Consistent with the glossary's གཏན་གྱི་འདུན་མ = 'mục tiêu lâu dài'.
p0155, མགོན་པོ་ཀླུ་སྒྲུབ = 'đấng Hộ Chủ Long Thọ'. ཀླུ་སྒྲུབ = Long Thọ is fixed; the epithet is new.
p0153, Kaniṣka verse: རྣམ་སྨིན་འབྱིན་པ་སྔོན་ལས.
p0155. Rendered literally; 'thiện/ác nghiệp' avoided because the Tibetan uses the colour metaphor.
p0155 verse. Short form of the glossary's འཛམ་བུའི་གླིང; same Vietnamese.
p0153, in the triad སྐྱབས་དང་མགོན་དང་དཔུང་གཉེན = 'chỗ nương tựa, đấng che chở và người thân trợ giúp'.
p0152, ཐག་གཅོད་པའི་ཞེ་དམ་མང་དུ་བྱ. Kadam idiom for a firmly-held inner resolve.

terms.kind: gap — ruling needed, wording kept under protest
terms.note: No entry exists for bare ལྷ, so the wording is kept per the gap rule, but I agree with the checker's substantive point and would not defend 'bổn tôn' if the ruling is made: p0154 ལྷ་དང་བླ་མ་ལ་གསོལ་བ་འདེབས is Kadampa prose and 'bổn tôn' = iṣṭadevatā = ཡི་དམ, a narrower and tantrically marked category than the syllable carries. A neutral 'đấng bổn tôn'-free rendering (e.g. 'chư thiên' is wrong here, but something like 'thiên tôn' / 'bổn tôn' has to be chosen deliberately) should be settled centrally. Same chunk, p0153 verse: ལྷ་གཅིག → 'đấng thiên tôn', which is a vocative address to a king and arguably a separate entry (ལྷ་གཅིག as royal address) rather than an inconsistency. Related existing entries that constrain the choice: ལྷ་བླ་མ (left in transcription), ལྷ་མིན, ལྷ་གཞན (p0064 verse). Recommend two entries: bare ལྷ, and ལྷ་གཅིག as an address.

p0155, མགོན་པོ་ཀླུ་སྒྲུབ་ཀྱིས → 'đấng Hộ Chủ Long Thọ'. No entry for མགོན་པོ as an honorific epithet before a master's name (ཀླུ་སྒྲུབ = 'Long Thọ' is correct per the fixed entry). Note the same syllable occurs in this chunk as a common noun in the triad at p0153, ཆོས་འབའ་ཞིག་སྐྱབས་དང་མགོན་དང་དཔུང་གཉེན་དུ་འགྱུར་ཚུལ → 'chỗ nương tựa, đấng che chở và người thân trợ giúp', so the entry should distinguish the epithet from the common noun ('đấng che chở').

p0153, first member of the same triad. No entry for the bare word, though it is high-frequency and heads the whole refuge section later in the book (སྐྱབས་འགྲོ), so it should be ruled on early — including whether the bare noun and the compound སྐྱབས་འགྲོ share a Vietnamese base.

NOT a translator error. Cited 2× in c048: p0152 རྣལ་འབྱོར་གྱི་དབང་ཕྱུག་ཤྲི་ཛ་ག་ཏ་མི་ཏྲ་ཨཱ་ནན་ཏས་ཀྱང → 'bậc Du-già Tự Tại Śrī Jagatamitra Ānanta'; p0153 ཤྲི་ཛ་ག་ཏ་མི་ཏྲས་ཀྱང → 'ngài Śrī Jagatamitra'. The two forms track the Tibetan, which itself writes ཨཱ་ནན་ཏ only on the first citation — the shorter second form is the source's, not a drift. Recommend one entry recording both forms plus the epithet རྣལ་འབྱོར་གྱི་དབང་ཕྱུག = 'bậc Du-già Tự Tại'. His work quoted here (the Candrarājalekha / letter to the king) is not named in the Tibetan and is deliberately not supplied.

The honorific of སྙིང་རྗེ, which glossary.json fixes as 'bi'. Occurs 8× in this chunk, several times in the SAME sentence-neighbourhood as སྙིང་རྗེ (p0182 line 1), so the two Tibetan words are now indistinguishable in Vietnamese. See flag — a ruling is needed on whether the honorific gets its own marking.

Twice in the phẩm Đế Giả verses (p0182). Deliberately NOT 'chúng sinh', because སེམས་ཅན (fixed) and འགྲོ་བ (provisional) already both hold that word and glossary.json flags that collision. 'quần sinh' (群生) is established Vietnamese Buddhist usage. Collapse it to 'chúng sinh' if a ruling prefers fewer words.

p0182, in the epithet སྟོབས་བཅུ་མངའ་བ = 'đấng có mười lực'. Standard Sino-Vietnamese would be 'thập lực'; kept numeral+noun so the epithet reads as a description, matching the glossary's treatment of དལ་འབྱོར.

Names the fourth of the Buddha's four qualities (སྐུ / གསུང་ / ཐུགས་ / འཕྲིན་ལས་ཀྱི་ཡོན་ཏན), so it is a section headword at p0182. 'sự nghiệp' rather than 'hạnh nghiệp' or 'sự nghiệp lợi sinh' — the Tibetan adds no object.

terms.vi: thành tựu một cách tự nhiên
terms.note: p0182, of the Buddha's activity of body/speech/mind. The Sino-Vietnamese 'nhậm vận thành tựu' is the alternative and may be preferable in a doctrinal register; chosen the transparent form because the term is not being defined here. See flag.
p0183, p0184. Follows the glossary's རྗེས་སུ་དྲན་པ = tùy niệm (recorded under བཀའ་དྲིན་རྗེས་སུ་དྲན་པ). Names the whole practice this section teaches.
p0184, Samādhirāja verse. Built on the glossary's ཐུབ་པ = 'đấng Mâu-ni' plus དབང་ = vương, on the precedent of མི་དབང = 'đấng nhân vương'.
p0184, Samādhirāja verse (རྒྱལ་བ་ཡི་ནི་སྐུ་བྱད). Honorific; the bodily form/features of the Buddha, paired against ཡེ་ཤེས in the same line.

p0184, Samādhirāja verse. འཇིག་རྟེན་ = thế gian per glossary; མགོན་པོ = đấng cứu hộ. Kept distinct from the proper name འཇིག་རྟེན་དབང་ཕྱུག = Thế Tự Tại, which glossary.json already notes must not take 'thế gian'.
p0183 (སྐྱབས་གསུམ་གྱི་ཡོན་ཏན). Rendered on the established སྐྱབས་འགྲོ = 'quy y' (c028, c040) rather than as 'Tam quy', so the link to the section's own verb སྐྱབས་སུ་འགྲོ་བ stays visible.
p0185, in the definition of the Jewel of Dharma (འགོག་པ་དང་ལམ་གྱི་བདེན་པ). Established Sino-Vietnamese.
p0185, same phrase. Established Sino-Vietnamese. Note glossary.json still has no entry for བདེན་པ generally — see the existing བདེན་པ་མཐོང་བ note.

p0182 verse, twice, including the compound སྲེད་པའི་འདོད་ཆགས where it stands beside འདོད་ཆགས (glossary: 'tham ái', provisional). 'khát ái' chosen precisely to keep the two apart, which is the collision the འདོད་ཆགས entry's own note predicted. A ruling should settle the pair together.
p0183, twice, as the positive member of the ཕུན་ཚོགས / རྒུད་པ pair. Distinct from the glossary's ཕུན་ཚོགས inside c005's 'dòng dõi viên mãn'.

p0185. NOT translated by guess: the form occurs 4× in the corpus (p0067, p0185, p0531, p0958) and in every case evaluates a quoted saying of a master, three of them followed by 'so one should do accordingly' or equivalent — i.e. a positive appraisal, 'apt / well said / to the point'. Recorded so a later chunk does not repair it to སྨད་པ ('đáng chê') , which would invert the sense in all four places.

p0183 (བསྒོམས་པས་འཕྲིག་ཚུད་ན); also p0145 (བསམས་པའི་འཕྲིག་ཚུད་པ་ཞིག་ལ). Sense taken from འཕྲིག་པ = lay động/rung động (cf. p0068 ཡིད་མི་འཕྲིག་པར) plus ཚུད་པ = nhập vào: the contemplation 'strikes home'. Deliberately NOT 'thấm vào tâm', which glossary.json already assigns to ཡིད་འཁུལ — a term that occurs in this same chunk at p0185. See flag.

p0185, Potowa (བློ་འགེལ་ལམ). One other corpus occurrence (དེ་དག་ལ་བློ་འགེལ་ན་མི་རུང). Sense: to place one's mind/reliance on something. Kept distinct from ཡིད་འཁུལ = 'thấm vào tâm' and from དད་པ = 'lòng tin'.
p0185, Potowa's simile (མོ་མ་རྣོ་ཤོས = 'thầy bói giỏi nhất'). རྣོ་ཤོས literally 'sharpest'.
p0184, Samādhirāja verse (ལུས་དང་ངག་དང་ཡིད་རབ་དང་བ་ཡིས). Kept distinct from the glossary's དད་པ = 'lòng tin' and མོས་པ = 'lòng tin ưa'.

p0164 (Śiṣyalekha verse) and p0159. IMPORTANT: source/clean prints this as ལོག་མ because CID 355 is an unrepaired ligature — see flags. Rendered 'cổ họng' here; c049 rendered the same word at p0159 as 'thực quản'. One of the two should be chosen in Phase 5.

p0165. Tibetan translation-name given back in Sanskrit (དགེ་འདུན = saṅgha, སྲུངས = rakṣita), following the glossary's practice for Śīlarakṣita / Dharmarakṣita. Not rendered by the Chinese-derived 'Tăng Hộ'.
p0165. The established Vietnamese for avadāna (譬喻), already used in the corpus for དཔེ (c016, c037: *Thí Dụ Pháp* of Potowa). Deliberately not transliterated 'A-ba-đà-na'.

p0165, cited as the source of the Vinayavastu (ལུང་གཞི) statement that the isolated hells lie near the shore of the great ocean. Title built from the two components; no settled Vietnamese title was found — see flag.
p0164, in the sūtra on the sesame-measure quoted in the Câu-xá Thích. ཁལ = a dry measure, rendered by the Sino-Vietnamese 'hộc'. སྦྱང་ is NOT separately rendered — see flag.

terms.vi: Bọng Nước / Bọng Nước Vỡ / Nứt Như Hoa Sen / Nứt Như Hoa Sen Lớn
terms.note: L37, L38, L42, L43. Names of four of the eight cold hells; none registered. Wording matches c050 L97-L104 exactly, so nothing changed. Pin as a set — the remaining four cold-hell names in c050 (Aṭaṭa/Hahava/Huhuva/Utpala and the rest of the list) should be registered in the same entry so the whole eight stay stable wherever the list recurs.

Neither registered; both Vietnamese forms already live elsewhere (thọ mạng: c045, c046, c047; thọ lượng: c047, c050). Proposed ruling, which this repair has already applied inside c051: bare ཚེ -> 'thọ mạng' (L36 ཚེ་ཡོངས་སུ་གཏུགས་པ, L45 ཚེ་དེ་ཙམ), ཚེའི་ཚད -> 'thọ lượng' (L27). Not a violation of any existing ruling — recorded so the split is deliberate and so a corpus sweep can check the earlier chunks against it.

L33, L35, in the Magadha sesame-measure simile (ཡུལ་མ་ག་དྷའི་ཏིལ་གྱི་སྦྱང་ཁལ་བརྒྱད་ཅུ་པ). Low priority: p0164 is the measure word's only occurrence so far, so nothing constrains it, but recording it now prevents divergence when the simile recurs. Note that 'thùng' is bracketed as a supplied classifier. ཡུལ་མ་ག་དྷ -> 'xứ Magadha' uses the registered མ་ག་དྷ = Magadha (provisional) and is correct.

terms.vi: Trình tự các điều cần học sau khi đã quy y
terms.note: Outline s074, path 6.2.3.1.1.2.1.4, level 7 → '#'. བསླབ་པར་བྱ་བ rendered with the glossary's བསླབ་བྱ = 'các điều cần học' so the section title and its four descendant headings (all built on བསླབ་བྱ) stay visibly one family.

terms.vi: Những điều rút ra từ bộ Nhiếp
terms.note: Outline s075, level 8 → '##'.

terms.vi: Những điều rút ra từ khẩu quyết
terms.note: Outline s076, level 8 → '##'. Uses the glossary's མན་ངག = khẩu quyết.

Outline s077, level 9 → '###'. Paired with ཐུན་མོང་གི་བསླབ་བྱ = 'các điều cần học chung', following the glossary precedent ཐུན་མོང་བ / ཐུན་མོང་མ་ཡིན་པ = 'phần chung / phần bất cộng' rather than the 'cộng thông' register, which is recorded for paths and vows.
Outline s080; named here only in the two-fold division on p0190. c061–c064 translate this section and should follow.

terms.vi: Các điều cần học thuộc phần ngăn cấm
terms.note: Outline s078, level 10 → '####'. Built on the 'phần X' pattern already used for ལུང་གི་བསྟན་པ / རྟོགས་པའི་བསྟན་པ. Deliberately not the Vinaya pair chỉ trì / tác trì, which the Tibetan does not use.

terms.vi: Các điều cần học thuộc phần thực hành
terms.note: Outline s079, level 10 → '####'. Note the source writes སྒྲུབ་པ in the heading and བསྒྲུབ་པ in the first line of the body; same Vietnamese for both. c060 continues this section and must match.
p0189–p0190, the two groups of four items from the Saṃgraha. Rendered plainly; there is no established Sino-Vietnamese for it.

terms.vi: thành tựu pháp tùy thuận với pháp
terms.note: p0189–p0190. Rendered componentially rather than with the fixed Sino-Vietnamese 'pháp tùy pháp hành', because the text immediately glosses the second ཆོས as niết-bàn and the gloss only reads if both occurrences of ཆོས are the same visible word.
p0189, ཆོས་མདོའི་སྡེ་ལ་སོགས་པ — the first of the twelve branches of scripture, named as the head of a list. Kept distinct from the general 'kinh'.

terms.vi: khiến các căn không buông lung
terms.note: p0190. The glossary's རྒོད་པ = 'trạo cử' is recorded for བྱིང་རྒོད, the meditative fault, and is NOT applied here: this རྒོད་པ is the senses running loose toward objects. Kept distinct from དབང་པོའི་སྒོ་སྡོམ་པ = 'thu thúc căn môn' (glossary), which is a different phrase in a different section.

p0190, p0191. Deliberately separated from གནོད་པ = 'tổn hại', because p0191 writes the pair གནོད་པ་དང་འཚེ་བ in one phrase and collapsing them would erase a distinction the source makes twice on the same page.
See the འཚེ་བ note — the two are kept apart on purpose.

p0191, འཇིག་རྟེན་པའི་ལྷ་དྲག་པོ་དང་ཁྱབ་འཇུག་སོགས. Left in Sanskrit, following the project's practice with Indian proper nouns (c005). Must NOT be rendered 'Tự Tại Thiên', which c055 already uses for a different Tibetan word. See flag.
p0191, paired with དྲག་པོ. Left in Sanskrit to match its pair-mate; the Sino-Vietnamese 'Biến Nhập thiên' would have no matching form for དྲག་པོ. See flag.
p0191, ཡི་དྭགས་སུ་གྱུར་པའི་གཞི་བདག་དང་ཀླུ — local/site deities who have fallen to the preta realm.
p0191, in the same phrase as གཞི་བདག.
p0191, in the simile of entrusting a patron with help for one's livelihood.
p0191, an example of contempt shown to a Buddha image. གཏའ་མ = pledge/collateral.
p0191, སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་གཟུགས་རི་མོར་བྲིས་པ. See flag on how the phrase is parsed.

p0190 l.15, མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ལས, at l.69 ('Trong *Niết-bàn* có nói'). Glossary registers མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ only as the term 'niết-bàn' (provisional); no kind:'title' entry exists, though decisions.md requires one fixed Vietnamese title per cited text at first occurrence. Note the source names no མདོ, so no 'Kinh' prefix was supplied (per the precedent in the སྡོང་པོ་བཀོད་པ and གསང་བ་བསམ་གྱིས་མི་ཁྱབ་པ notes).
p0190 l.15 verse and p0191 l.1, at l.78 and l.81. No entry; consistent with c005/c007/c058/c063 corpus usage. Gap only.

p0189 l.9, དམ་པ་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཉན་ཐོས, at l.36 ('bậc chân nhân là đức Phật'). The glossary fixes the phrase སྐྱེས་བུ་དམ་པ = 'bậc chân nhân' (used correctly at l.29 for the section headword). Extending the same Vietnamese to a bare attributive དམ་པ is unruled, and it makes the section headword and an ordinary adjective read identically two paragraphs apart. Compare བཤེས་གཉེན་དམ་པ, where དམ་པ was ruled 'chân chính'. A ruling is needed; on the existing precedent 'đức Phật chân chính' or 'bậc chân chính là đức Phật' would be the parallel form, so this was left unchanged rather than re-decided here.

p0206, སྲིད་པའི་ཟུག་རྔུ་གཅོད་བྱེད་ལམ = 'con đường cắt đứt gai nhọn của hữu'. No occurrence anywhere in the translated corpus and no glossary entry; the word recurs at p0288, p0498, p0532, so it needs a ruling. 'gai nhọn' chosen over 'mũi tên' because the verb is གཅོད (cut), which suits a thorn rather than a dart. སྲིད་པ = hữu follows the existing provisional entry.

terms.vi: không tuyên xưng [chỗ quy y] nào khác
terms.note: The fourth of the four factors of having gone for refuge (བསྡུ་བ list at p0179), referred back to at p0206. Defined at p0187 as knowing the superiority of the inner over the outer teacher/teaching/followers and taking refuge in the Three Jewels alone. The bracketed [chỗ quy y] supplies what the Tibetan leaves implicit. WARNING: the chunks covering p0179 and p0187 (c057-c058) are not yet translated, so whichever of us goes first fixes this term — cross-check required.

Of the refuge vow: གཏོང་བ = outright abandoning it, ཉམས་པ = its degeneration. The whole of p0206's first half turns on keeping the two apart (some masters count six transgressions as གཏོང་བ, some nine, the rest being only ཉམས་པའི་རྒྱུ). No entry exists for either.

terms.vi: điều cần học riêng biệt / điều cần học chung
terms.note: The two classes of refuge precept; ཐུན་མོང་གི་བསླབ་བྱ is this chunk's own section heading (s080). Built on the glossary's provisional བསླབ་བྱ = 'các điều cần học' plus ཐུན་མོང་བ = 'cộng thông'/'chung'. 'chung' preferred over 'cộng thông' here because the contrast is with སོ་སོ (individual), not with a vehicle.

p0206 (སྐྱབས་ལ་བློ་མ་ཁེལ་བས, negated) and p0201 (དཀོན་མཆོག་ལ་བློ་ཁེལ་བར་བྱའོ). Kept distinct from དད་པ = 'lòng tin' and མོས་པ = 'lòng tin ưa', both already in the glossary; བློ་ཁེལ་བ is entrusting/relying rather than faith.

l.38. glossary.json has only the chapter entries ཐོས་པའི་ཚོམས = Phẩm Văn and མཛའ་བཤེས་ཀྱི་ཚོམས / བཤེས་ཀྱི་ཚོམས = Phẩm Thân Hữu; nothing for bare ཚོམས. Wording kept: it matches established corpus practice (c044, c045, c047, c065, c079 all render ཚོམས་ལས as "Pháp Tập Yếu Tụng"). A central ruling is needed registering bare ཚོམས = the whole Udānavarga = "Pháp Tập Yếu Tụng", explicitly distinct from the X-varga chapter pattern, whose note says "the text names only the chapter, so only the chapter is named in Vietnamese" — that note reads as forbidding exactly this expansion, so the two must be separated by rule rather than left to be inferred.

terms.vi: quy y  ·  thọ trì quy y  ·  chỗ quy y
terms.note: No glossary.json entry at all, despite these being the pivot terms of the section (སྐྱབས appears 9× on p0206). Renderings kept unchanged: internally consistent here and matching c055, c058, c063. Registering should cover all three forms, including the nominal སྐྱབས = "chỗ quy y" (the refuge as object/protector, ll.20, 23, 36-38) as distinct from the act.

l.22, དེ་དག་དང་མི་མཐུན་པའི་སྟོན་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ — teachers discordant with the Three Jewels. glossary.json registers སྟོན་པ = "đấng Đạo Sư" as an epithet of the Buddha only. The lowercase "bậc đạo sư" here correctly keeps the two senses apart and matches c063's "bậc đạo sư xấu", but nothing licenses the split, so a consistency sweep could read it as drift. Needs an entry recording: Buddha sense = "đấng Đạo Sư"; generic/non-Buddhist sense = "bậc đạo sư", lowercase.

Cited twice on p0186 (the first occurrence straddles the p0185/p0186 boundary, so its opening words fell in c057). Established Sino-Vietnamese title 法集經. NOT verified against an existing Vietnamese edition.
Udbhaṭasiddhasvāmin's hymn; cited twice on p0188. Full Tibetan form is ཁྱད་པར་དུ་འཕགས་པའི་བསྟོད་པ. Sino-Vietnamese 殊勝讚. Vietnamese form not verified against an existing edition — see flags.

p0187. Built from the Tibetan components, following the glossary's ཤེས་རབ་སྒྲོན་མེའི་རྒྱ་ཆེར་འགྲེལ་པ = 'Bát-nhã Đăng Luận Quảng Thích' (རྒྱ་ཆེར་འགྲེལ = Quảng Thích) and འདུལ་བ = Luật. Underlying Sanskrit work not verified.
